title: Inherited characteristics
keyIdea: Plants and animals get some of their features from their parents. A feature passed on from parents to their young is called an inherited characteristic, or trait, such as ear shape, fur colour or eye colour. Young are like their parents, but they are not exact copies, and brothers and sisters differ from each other. These small differences between living things of the same kind are called variation. Things that happen during a life, like an injury or a learned trick, are not inherited.
familyTip: Look at family photos together, or at a litter of kittens or puppies if you know someone with one. Spot features the young share with their parents, like hair colour or ear shape, and ways they differ from each other. Then talk about which things were learned or happened later, like riding a bike or a scar, and agree that those are not passed on.

visual.caption: Was it passed on from the parents, or did it happen during life? Drag each card to a box, or tap the card then a box.

items: A puppy's spotty fur, like its mum's
The shape of a cat's ears
The colour of a flower's petals
A scar from falling off a bike
A dog that has learned to fetch

lab.caption: Flagship lab: find a baby rabbit's parents, sort features into inherited or not, breed a litter that varies, then measure ten sunflowers into a bar chart.

kid: Living things have babies of the same kind. Rabbits have baby rabbits, and sunflower seeds grow into sunflowers. Babies get some of their features from their parents. A feature passed on from parents is called inherited. Ear shape, fur colour and eye colour are inherited.

Babies look like their parents, but they are not exact copies. In one litter, some rabbits may be brown and some white. Some are a little bigger than others. These small differences are called variation.

Plants vary too. Plant ten seeds from one sunflower. They will not all grow to the same height. If you measure them and make a bar chart, most may be near one height, with some a bit shorter and some a bit taller.

Some things are not inherited. A rabbit that tears its ear in a fight will still have babies with normal ears. A dog that learns a trick will not have puppies that already know it. These things happen during a life, so they are not passed on.
adult: Ages 8 to 9 (NGSS 3-LS3-1). Children use data as evidence that plants and animals inherit traits from their parents, and that traits vary in a group of the same kind. This builds towards NC Year 6: offspring vary and are not identical to their parents. Key words are inherited, trait (or characteristic), offspring and variation. Genes and DNA can wait.

Common mistakes: thinking young are exact copies of a parent; thinking brothers and sisters should look the same; and thinking a baby takes after only one parent, when it gets traits from both. Many children also think injuries, haircuts or learned skills are passed on. Some think a group that varies cannot all be the same kind.

The data part matters. Children collect or read measurements of one kind of living thing, such as the heights of sunflowers grown from one plant's seeds. A bar chart shows most values bunched near the middle, with some spread either side. That spread is the evidence of variation. Sun, water and food also cause some of it, which later lessons cover.

In the lab your child picks the parents a baby rabbit got its floppy ears and brown fur from. Then they sort six features into inherited and not inherited. Next, two parents have six babies: all have floppy ears, but fur and size vary. Last, they measure ten sunflowers into a bar chart and find the most common height.

choices: Passed on from parents to their young
Learned by practising
Caused by an accident
practice.hint: Think about the floppy-eared rabbit. Where did its ears come from?
practice.explain: An inherited trait is passed on from parents to their young, like the baby rabbit's floppy ears. Learned skills and injuries are not inherited.

practice.prompt: A rabbit has a litter of {n} babies. {b} of them are brown and the rest are white. How many are white?
practice.hint: Take the brown babies away from the whole litter.
practice.explain: {n} − {b} = {=n-b}. {=n-b} babies are white. Same parents, but the babies vary in fur colour.

practice.prompt: A dog lost part of her tail in an accident. What will her puppies' tails be like?
choices: Normal tails
Short tails like hers
No tails at all
practice.hint: Did the short tail come from her parents, or did it happen during her life?
practice.explain: The accident happened during her life, so it is not inherited. Her puppies are born with normal tails.

practice.prompt: The tallest sunflower from one packet of seeds is {t} cm. The shortest is {s} cm. How many centimetres taller is the tallest one?
practice.hint: Take the shortest height away from the tallest.
practice.explain: {t} − {s} = {=t-s} cm. Sunflowers of the same kind still vary in height.

practice.prompt: Ten sunflowers grown from one plant's seeds are all different heights. What does this show?
choices: Living things of the same kind vary
Some of them are not sunflowers
Someone measured them wrong
practice.hint: Remember the bar chart: most were near one height, with some shorter and some taller.
practice.explain: They are all sunflowers. Plants of the same kind are not all identical: this is variation.

pool.prompt: Which of these is an inherited characteristic of a cat?
choices: The colour of its fur
Knowing where its food bowl is
A scratch on its nose
pool.hint: Which one was there when the kitten was born?
pool.explain: Fur colour is passed on from the parents. Knowing where the bowl is was learned, and a scratch happened during its life.

pool.prompt: A dog learns to sit when she is told. Will her puppies know how to sit without being taught?
choices: No, learned skills are not inherited
Yes, she passes it on
Only if they look like her
pool.hint: Was she born knowing how to sit?
pool.explain: Sitting is a learned skill. It is not passed on, so each puppy has to be taught.

pool.prompt: Two brown rabbits have five babies. What is most likely?
choices: They are all rabbits, but not all exactly the same
They are all exactly the same
Some of them will be kittens
pool.hint: Think of the litter in the lab.
pool.explain: Rabbits have baby rabbits, and the babies are like their parents. But they vary a little, so they are not all identical.

pool.prompt: A gardener plants {n} seeds from one sunflower. {a} grow taller than 170 cm. How many do not?
pool.hint: Take the tall ones away from all the plants.
pool.explain: {n} − {a} = {=n-a}. The plants all came from one sunflower, but their heights vary.

choices: Differences between living things of the same kind
When a baby is an exact copy of its parent
When an animal learns something new
pool.hint: Think about how the six babies in the litter looked.
pool.explain: Variation means living things of the same kind are a bit different from each other, like rabbits with different fur.

pool.prompt: A baby rabbit has floppy ears. Which pair are most likely its parents?
choices: Two rabbits with floppy ears
Two rabbits with ears that stand up
Any two rabbits, ears do not matter
pool.hint: Ear shape is inherited. Where could the floppy ears come from?
pool.explain: Ear shape is passed on from parents, so the parents most likely have floppy ears too.

pool.prompt: Ten sunflower heights: 150, 160, 160, 170, 170, 170, 170, 180, 180, 190 cm. Which height is the most common?
choices: 170 cm
190 cm
150 cm
pool.hint: Count how many times each height appears. Which bar would be tallest?
pool.explain: 170 cm appears 4 times, more than any other height, so its bar is the tallest. 190 cm is the tallest plant, not the most common height.

pool.prompt: Sam says he got his curly hair only from his dad. What is a better way to say it?
choices: He inherits traits from both his parents
Hair is never inherited
He chose to have curly hair
pool.hint: How many parents pass on traits to a baby?
pool.explain: Young get traits from both parents. He may look more like his dad in one feature, but traits come from both.

pool.prompt: In a class, {g} children have brown eyes and {b} have blue eyes. How many children are there in all?
pool.explain: {g} + {b} = {=g+b}. Eye colour is inherited, and it varies from child to child.
